message.content:
### Your Rights as a Tenant in Texas (as of 2026) | Area | What You’re Entitled To | How to Exercise It | |------|------------------------|--------------------| | **Security Deposit** | • The landlord may charge up to **one month’s rent** for a furnished unit and **two months’ rent** for an unfurnished unit.
• The deposit must be returned within **30 days** after you move out, minus any lawful deductions. | • Keep a written move‑in inspection report.
• Request a written itemized statement of deductions if the landlord withholds any portion. | | **Habitability** | • The landlord must keep the premises in a safe, sanitary, and livable condition (e.g., plumbing, heating, electrical, structural integrity). | • Report problems in writing (email or certified mail).
• If the landlord fails to fix, you may withhold rent, repair and deduct, or file a complaint with the Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA). | | **Rent Payment** | • Rent is due on the date specified in the lease; late fees are allowed only if stated in the lease and not excessive. | • Keep receipts or bank records. | | **Entry Rights** | • Landlord must give **at least 24 hours’ written notice** before entering, except in emergencies. | • Keep a log of all entries. | | **Privacy** | • You have the right to quiet enjoyment; the landlord cannot harass or interfere with your use of the property. | • Document any harassment and consider filing a complaint. | | **Discrimination** | • Landlords cannot discriminate based on race, color, religion, sex, national origin, disability, familial status, or source of income (e.g., Section 8). | • File a complaint with the Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR) if you suspect discrimination. | | **Lease Termination** | • Either party may terminate a month‑to‑month lease with **30 days’ written notice**.
• For fixed‑term leases, the landlord must provide a valid reason for early termination (e.g., breach of lease). | • Provide written notice and keep copies. | | **Repair and Deduct** | • If the landlord fails to repair a major issue, you may repair it yourself and deduct the cost from rent, provided you follow the proper procedure. | • Keep receipts and give the landlord a written notice of intent to repair and deduct. | | **Eviction Process** | • The landlord must serve a **30‑day notice** for nonpayment of rent or a **60‑day notice** for lease violations.
• After the notice period, the landlord can file an eviction lawsuit. | • Respond to the lawsuit, attend court, and present evidence of compliance or defenses. | | **Fair Housing** | • Landlords must comply with federal Fair Housing Act and Texas Fair Housing Act. | • Report violations to TCHR or the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development (HUD). | | **Utilities** | • The lease should specify which utilities you are responsible for. | • Verify utility responsibilities at move‑in. | | **Maintenance Responsibilities** | • Tenants must keep the unit clean and free of damage beyond normal wear and tear. | • Keep records of maintenance requests and responses. | | **Subletting** | • Subletting is allowed only if the lease permits it or the landlord consents. | • Obtain written consent before subletting. | | **Legal Assistance** | • Texas offers free or low‑cost legal aid for tenants (e.g., Texas Legal Services Center, local bar associations). | • Contact a local tenant advocacy group or legal aid office. | #### Quick Steps If You Encounter Problems 1. **Document Everything** – Keep copies of the lease, correspondence, photos, and receipts. 2. **Notify the Landlord in Writing** – Use certified mail or email with read receipt. 3. **Know the Timeframes** – Texas law sets specific notice periods for repairs, entry, and eviction. 4. **Seek Mediation** – Many counties offer mediation services for landlord‑tenant disputes. 5. **File a Complaint** – If unresolved, file with TDHCA, TCHR, or the local court. #### Useful Resources - **Texas Department of Housing and Community Affairs (TDHCA)** – [tdhca.texas.gov](https://tdhca.texas.gov) - **Texas Commission on Human Rights (TCHR)** – [tchr.texas.gov](https://tchr.texas.gov) - **Texas Legal Services Center** – [texaslegalservices.org](https://texaslegalservices.org) - **Local Bar Association** – Many offer free tenant counseling. --- **Disclaimer:** This information is general in nature and not legal advice. For specific situations, consult a licensed attorney or a local tenant advocacy organization.
